name: American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius)
short: A small randomised trial in healthy volunteers found American ginseng reduced warfarin's anticoagulant effect. In two placebo-controlled trials, reported toxicities did not differ between groups.
text: In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 20 healthy volunteers, two weeks of American ginseng significantly lowered the peak INR and plasma warfarin levels, and the authors concluded that American ginseng reduces warfarin's anticoagulant effect and that physicians prescribing warfarin should ask about ginseng use; they noted as a limitation that participants were young, healthy volunteers rather than patients taking therapeutic doses of warfarin. On general tolerability, a multisite double-blind trial in 364 cancer survivors found that toxicities, by self-report and by clinician grading, did not differ significantly between American ginseng and placebo over 8 weeks. A small randomised trial in children aged 3 to 12 years with upper respiratory tract infection (46 randomised) reported no serious adverse events, and the frequency and severity of adverse events did not differ significantly between the two ginseng dosing arms and placebo.
